alignments.note: Substantival article takes the supplied pronoun and relative *Those that*, headed on the pronoun (rule 41).
The adjective keeps its own English with the supplied copula (rules 41, 20).
Second substantival article with its own written *those that* (rule 41).
Adjective with the supplied copula, headed on *far*.
Verb with its auxiliary, headed on *mock*.
The ASV promotes the prepositional object to a bare direct object, leaving the preposition nothing (rule 40).
Suffix rendered by the object pronoun *thee*.

טְמֵאַת הַשֵּׁם (the marginal gloss *defiled of name*) is rendered by the single English expression *infamous one*, of which no morpheme owns a part, so the three morphemes share one unit under rule 30; the vocative *thou* joins the noun's unit under rule 36 and the head falls on the lexeme-bearing *infamous* (rule 31). The competing reading aligns the article and שֵׁם separately and marks them unrepresented.
The ASV's marked *and* has no waw in this clause to license it; count the conjunctions against the connectives as rule 42 directs, and the surplus is added (rule 30).
The ASV writes no *the* for this phrase (rule 29).
Nomen rectum takes the relational *of* under rule 19.

review_notes: The vocative pair is read as one fused rendering for the first phrase and as an ordinary construct for the second, since the ASV spends a word on each part of רַבַּת הַמְּהוּמָה but not of טְמֵאַת הַשֵּׁם.
